marta: rolling out quartz8b-lite to canary and seeing big tail spikes at ~120-150ms per-token while most tokens stay ~12ms. also two soft OOMs on a few nodes :confused:
devin: can you paste the exact workload? batch size / max_new_tokens / pref etc?
marta: tests: batching=dynamic, target_batch_tokens=4096, max_new_tokens=512, prefetch=true. repro on a3.16xlarge with 80GB cards.
nashok: interesting — quartz8b has a custom rotary implementation. last time we saw kernel mismatch it caused PTX fallback on certain seq lengths. might explain spikes.
zoe: @marta can you run the kernel tracer on one of the bad runs? `INFER_TRACE=kernels ./run_canary.sh` should show hot kernels.
marta: pasted output (trimmed):
```
KERNEL_PROFILE:
 aten_attention_rotary  72%  (avg 9.8ms, tail 145ms)
 matmul_bmm          12%  (avg 3.1ms)
 kv_read             8%   (avg 1.2ms)
 mem_alloc/defrag    6%   (tail spikes ~120ms)
```
devin: that aten_attention_rotary tail matches kernel fallback suspicion. which cuDNN/CUDA version on that fleet?
marta: CUDA 12.1, driver 545.xx, cuDNN 9.4.0. we just rolled driver last week.
nashok: older rotary kernel path was compiled for CUDA 11.x optimizations. when run under 12.1 it can fall back to a slower generic kernel. combine that with fragmentation (mem_alloc shows defrag) and you get a high-latency tail.
zoe: quick mitigation — pin max_new_tokens to 256 on canary and force kernel to use fused rotary by toggling model build flag `ROTARY_FORCE_FUSED=1` in runtime config. also reduce target_batch_tokens to 2048 for now.
marta: doing that now. scheduling canary change in 2min.
sre-bot: deploy canary job quartz8b-lite/2021 applied by marta — state: starting :rocket:
(marta edits config)
marta: updated: max_new_tokens=256, target_batch_tokens=2048, env ROTARY_FORCE_FUSED=1, prefetch=false for canary.
zoe: keep an eye on mem_alloc tail. if defrag events continue we need to do a KV-prefetch slot shrink (slot_compactor tweak) or bump early-eviction threshold.
devin: also add a kernel compatibility check in model onboarding pipeline: run a short kernel-bench step that tests rotary kernels across our cuda/driver combos. Fail fast on fallback.
nashok: agreed. I'll add a lightweight kernel probe in CI that runs random seq lengths 1..1024 and checks which kernel is selected. If fallback, fail and log suggested flags.
marta: canary is green so far, tail reduced to 18ms and no OOMs after the change :tada:
zoe: excellent. followups: (1) add probe to onboarding CI, (2) update runtime docs about ROTARY_FORCE_FUSED, (3) schedule fleet driver rollback/next-driver validation window.
marta: filing followup ticket with notes and config snippets. thanks all. :heart:
